name: Pale Oak
lede: Pale Oak is an English translation of a traditional Japanese name, Aoshirotsurubami, a muted sage green named for an oak-dyed cloth.

sections.title: A Japanese dye word in English
sections.body:
ColorHub's library carries this swatch under the working name Dusty Sage, with Aoshirotsurubami (青白橡, "pale oak") listed as its Japanese source name [1]. *Tsurubami* names dye from acorns and oak bark, a staple of old Japanese textile dyeing, and *ao-shiro* ("blue-white") marks this as the paler, cooler member of the tsurubami family [1]. ColorHub's English title translates that name directly rather than keeping the Japanese word as the headline, in line with the library's English-first naming rule [1]. A deeper tsurubami, without the ao-shiro qualifier, would read as a warmer, darker oak-bark brown rather than this cool pale green [1].

The nearest everyday name on file is [[sage]], about 4.2 units of ΔE away [1]. [[moss]], [[fern-green|Fern Green]] and [[khaki]] sit in the same muted-green family [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Pale Oak in 503 of 23,781 paintings (2.12 percent), as photographed, mostly as a highlight [2]. It peaks in the 1940s, in 5 of 28 paintings, at over eight times the archive's overall rate for that decade, and it is strongly over-represented in Impressionist painting, more than five times the archive average [2]. It keeps company with Sage, Viridian and Ash more than chance [2]. These are screen approximations of aged, varnished canvases, not pigment identifications [2].
